name: Orchestrator
desc: Breaks the top-level goal into subtasks and decides which agent or tool handles each one.
core: Decomposes user goals into an execution plan
Routes subtasks to the right sub-agent or tool
Tracks overall task state and sequencing

risks.name: Goal manipulation via prompt injection
risks.impact: An attacker rewrites the plan the orchestrator is working from, silently redirecting the entire system toward their own objective instead of the user's.
risks.mitigation: Separate trusted instructions from untrusted content; validate plans against an allow-listed goal schema before execution.

risks.name: Infinite loop / resource exhaustion
risks.impact: A malformed or adversarial plan causes the orchestrator to keep re-delegating the same subtask, burning compute and API budget.
risks.mitigation: Enforce hard step/time/cost budgets per task and detect repeated subtask signatures.

risks.name: Single point of failure
risks.impact: Because every agent depends on it, compromising or crashing the orchestrator takes down or misdirects the whole system at once.
risks.mitigation: Add plan-integrity checks, redundancy, and circuit breakers so a single bad plan can't cascade.

risks.name: Insecure delegation logic
risks.impact: Weak rules for choosing which agent gets a subtask let an attacker steer sensitive work toward a weaker or compromised agent.
risks.mitigation: Base delegation on verified capability and trust tiers, not on agent self-reported claims.

name: Sub-Agents
desc: Specialized agents that carry out the subtasks the orchestrator assigns.
core: Executes a narrow, specialized subtask
Reports results back up to the orchestrator
May invoke tools or call other agents directly

risks.name: Role confusion / impersonation
risks.impact: A malicious message convinces one agent it is actually another, trusted agent, causing it to accept instructions it should reject.
risks.mitigation: Give every agent a signed, verifiable identity that other agents check before trusting a message.

risks.name: Excessive agency
risks.impact: An agent is granted broader permissions than its task requires, so a single manipulated instruction can trigger high-impact actions like sending money or deleting data.
risks.mitigation: Scope each agent's permissions tightly to the minimum needed for its specific role, and re-evaluate scope per task.

risks.name: Insecure inter-agent trust
risks.impact: Agents accept output from other agents at face value, so one manipulated agent can quietly poison the reasoning of every agent downstream.
risks.mitigation: Treat inter-agent messages as untrusted input and apply the same validation used for external data.

name: Tool-Calling Layer
desc: The interface agents use to call external functions, APIs, and code.
core: Exposes a catalog of callable tools/functions to agents
Executes the tool call and returns results
Enforces (or should enforce) permission boundaries per tool

risks.name: Tool poisoning
risks.impact: A malicious or compromised tool definition includes hidden instructions that hijack the calling agent the moment the tool is invoked.
risks.mitigation: Pin tool definitions, verify their source/signature, and diff them against a known-good baseline before use.

risks.name: Arbitrary code execution
risks.impact: A code-execution tool lets an attacker-controlled instruction run unrestricted code on the host system.
risks.mitigation: Run tool execution inside a hardened sandbox with no default access to secrets, network, or the filesystem.

risks.name: Unvalidated trust in tool output
risks.impact: Agents treat whatever a tool returns as ground truth, so a spoofed or manipulated tool response can steer later reasoning unchecked.
risks.mitigation: Validate and type-check tool outputs before they re-enter the agent's context.

name: Memory / Context Store
desc: Persists conversation history, long-term memory, and embeddings across turns and sessions.
core: Stores conversation and task history
Retrieves relevant past context for new tasks
Often shared across multiple agents or sessions

risks.name: Memory poisoning
risks.impact: An attacker writes malicious content into long-term memory once, and it keeps influencing agent behavior across every future session that reads it.
risks.mitigation: Validate and provenance-tag anything written to persistent memory; treat recalled memory as untrusted input.

risks.name: Cross-session data leakage
risks.impact: Context meant for one user or task bleeds into another session, exposing private data to the wrong party.
risks.mitigation: Strictly partition memory stores per user/tenant with enforced access boundaries.

risks.name: Persistent prompt injection
risks.impact: A prompt injection is stored rather than transient, so it keeps firing every time that memory is recalled, long after the original interaction.
risks.mitigation: Sanitize content before storage and periodically re-validate stored memory against current policy.

name: Inter-Agent Comms
desc: The channel agents use to pass messages, requests, and results to one another.
core: Routes messages between agents
Carries task handoffs and intermediate results
Coordinates multi-agent workflows

risks.name: Message spoofing
risks.impact: An attacker crafts a message that appears to come from a trusted agent, getting other agents to act on forged instructions.
risks.mitigation: Sign inter-agent messages and verify sender identity before acting on message content.

risks.name: Man-in-the-middle injection
risks.impact: A party intercepts the message bus and injects or alters instructions in transit between two legitimate agents.
risks.mitigation: Encrypt and authenticate the transport layer end to end between agents.

risks.name: Lack of message integrity checks
risks.impact: Without checksums or signatures, corrupted or subtly altered messages pass through unnoticed and change downstream behavior.
risks.mitigation: Add integrity verification (hashes/signatures) on every inter-agent message.

name: Retrieval / RAG
desc: Fetches external documents or data to ground agent responses in current information.
core: Searches a knowledge base or the web for relevant content
Injects retrieved passages into the agent's context
Cites or grounds responses in retrieved material

risks.name: Indirect prompt injection via retrieved content
risks.impact: A document the system retrieves contains hidden instructions that the agent follows as if the user had typed them.
risks.mitigation: Isolate retrieved content as data, not instructions, and strip or flag embedded imperative language.

risks.name: Data poisoning of the knowledge base
risks.impact: An attacker seeds the retrieval corpus itself, so future queries reliably surface manipulated content.
risks.mitigation: Control write-access to the knowledge base and monitor it for anomalous or injected content.

risks.name: Source spoofing
risks.impact: Retrieved content is presented as authoritative when its actual source cannot be verified, misleading both the agent and the end user.
risks.mitigation: Track and surface provenance for every retrieved passage.

name: Execution Sandbox
desc: Isolates code execution, browsing, and file operations from the host and from other agents.
core: Runs agent-initiated code or scripts in isolation
Restricts filesystem, network, and process access
Should contain the blast radius of any single compromised action

risks.name: Sandbox escape
risks.impact: A flaw in the isolation layer lets agent-executed code break out and act directly on the host system.
risks.mitigation: Use hardened, regularly patched isolation technology and least-privilege container configuration.

risks.name: Privilege escalation
risks.impact: Code running in the sandbox finds a path to elevate its own permissions beyond what was granted.
risks.mitigation: Run sandboxed processes as non-root with no unnecessary capabilities, and audit for escalation paths.

risks.name: Insufficient isolation between agents
risks.impact: Multiple agents share a runtime environment, so one compromised agent can read or tamper with another's execution.
risks.mitigation: Give each agent (or task) its own isolated execution context rather than a shared runtime.

name: External Integrations
desc: Connections to outside services — email, calendars, payments, ticketing, and more.
core: Lets agents take real-world action through third-party services
Authenticates to external platforms on the system's behalf
Expands what the agent system can actually do

risks.name: Over-permissioned API scopes
risks.impact: Integrations are granted far more access than any given task needs, so a manipulated agent can take actions well outside its intended purpose.
risks.mitigation: Request the narrowest OAuth/API scopes possible and review them regularly.

risks.name: Third-party supply chain compromise
risks.impact: A vulnerability or breach at the integrated service propagates directly into your agent system through the trusted connection.
risks.mitigation: Vet integration partners, monitor advisories, and limit blast radius with scoped credentials.

risks.name: Data exfiltration via a legitimate channel
risks.impact: An attacker uses a legitimate, already-authorized integration (e.g. email or file-sharing) to quietly move sensitive data out — traffic that looks completely normal.
risks.mitigation: Monitor outbound data volume/destination patterns on integrations, not just their authorization status.

name: Credentials & Secrets
desc: API keys, tokens, and service credentials that let agents authenticate to tools and integrations.
core: Stores and issues credentials agents need to act
Authenticates agents to tools, APIs, and services
Often shared across multiple agents for convenience

risks.name: Secret leakage via logs or output
risks.impact: A credential ends up in a debug log, error message, or model output, giving anyone who can read that output the keys themselves.
risks.mitigation: Scrub secrets from logs and outputs automatically; never place raw credentials in prompts or context.

risks.name: Long-lived static credentials
risks.impact: Credentials that never expire remain useful to an attacker indefinitely once stolen, with no natural window of exposure.
risks.mitigation: Use short-lived, automatically rotated tokens instead of static keys.

risks.name: Credential reuse across agents
risks.impact: The same key is shared by many agents, so compromising the weakest one gives an attacker access everywhere that key works.
risks.mitigation: Issue distinct, narrowly scoped credentials per agent so compromise doesn't generalize.

name: Human-in-the-Loop
desc: Checkpoints where a person reviews or approves an agent's proposed action before it executes.
core: Presents a proposed high-stakes action for human review
Blocks execution until approval is given
Provides an accountability checkpoint in the workflow

risks.name: Approval fatigue / rubber-stamping
risks.impact: When approval requests are frequent and repetitive, reviewers start clicking approve out of habit rather than genuine review.
risks.mitigation: Reserve human review for genuinely high-risk actions and make requests specific enough to actually evaluate.

risks.name: Bypassable confirmation step
risks.impact: The approval step can be routed around programmatically, for instance by an agent calling a lower-level function that skips the check entirely.
risks.mitigation: Enforce approval at the permission layer itself, not just in the conversational flow that's easy to sidestep.

risks.name: Unclear accountability
risks.impact: When something goes wrong, it's unclear whether the human approver, the agent, or the system designer is responsible for the outcome.
risks.mitigation: Log exactly what was shown to the approver at decision time, not just that approval occurred.

name: Agent Identity & AuthZ
desc: Issues, verifies, scopes, and revokes agent identities and delegated authority for actions.
core: Assigns verifiable identities to agents
Authorizes sensitive actions per task and context
Revokes or constrains delegated authority when risk changes

risks.name: Rogue agent registration
risks.impact: An attacker enrolls an untrusted agent into the environment and makes it appear legitimate to orchestrators, tools, or other agents.
risks.mitigation: Require signed registration, verified ownership, approval workflows, and continuous inventory reconciliation for agent identities.

risks.name: Broken delegated authorization
risks.impact: An agent receives authority from another agent without a task-bound policy check, allowing privilege to spread beyond the original intent.
risks.mitigation: Bind delegated permissions to task, actor, time, data scope, and action type; re-check authorization at every sensitive call.

risks.name: Stale or revoked token reuse
risks.impact: A token that should no longer be trusted still works, letting compromised agents continue acting after deactivation or scope changes.
risks.mitigation: Use short-lived tokens, revocation checks, audience binding, and continuous token introspection.

name: Agent Skills / MCP Registry
desc: Reusable skills, MCP servers, manifests, and workflow packages that define what agents can do and how they do it.
core: Publishes and installs reusable agent skills or MCP servers
Declares permissions, handlers, scripts, and workflow behavior
Updates behavior packages over time

risks.name: Malicious skill or MCP package installation
risks.impact: A skill, plugin, or MCP server embeds harmful behavior that is trusted as reusable agent capability after installation.
risks.mitigation: Install only from verified publishers; scan behavior, scripts, manifests, and natural-language instructions before activation.

risks.name: Skill typosquatting / brand impersonation
risks.impact: A look-alike skill name or publisher tricks users or agents into installing an attacker-controlled package.
risks.mitigation: Verify publisher identity, package signing, reputation, namespace ownership, and exact dependency names.

risks.name: Unsigned or unpinned skill update
risks.impact: A previously safe skill silently changes behavior after an update, turning an approved capability into a supply-chain foothold.
risks.mitigation: Pin versions, require signed updates, diff manifests and instructions, and stage updates before production use.

name: Context Boundary & Provenance
desc: Separates instructions from data and preserves evidence, source, and trust level as context moves across agents and tools.
core: Labels context by source, trust level, and purpose
Prevents data from being promoted into instructions
Preserves provenance across memory, RAG, tools, and outputs

risks.name: Context boundary collapse
risks.impact: Untrusted data is treated as an instruction, policy, or trusted state, allowing an attacker to steer agent behavior indirectly.
risks.mitigation: Use explicit context labels and enforce instruction/data separation before model invocation and tool execution.

risks.name: Provenance loss across hops
risks.impact: As content moves through RAG, memory, tools, and agents, the system loses where it came from and why it should be trusted.
risks.mitigation: Carry provenance metadata with every context fragment and block trust elevation without verification.

risks.name: Evidence laundering through summaries
risks.impact: A false or malicious claim becomes credible after being summarized, cached, or cited by another agent.
risks.mitigation: Link summaries back to original evidence, distinguish claims from verified facts, and require source-level validation.

name: Model / Inference Routing
desc: Selects model, prompt template, policy tier, context window, and fallback behavior for agent reasoning.
core: Routes tasks to models or providers
Applies prompt templates and system policies
Handles fallback, retry, and long-running reasoning behavior

risks.name: Unsafe model fallback
risks.impact: A failed or overloaded primary model falls back to a weaker model or policy tier without preserving safety constraints.
risks.mitigation: Define approved fallback tiers and require policy equivalence checks before automatic failover.

risks.name: Prompt template injection
risks.impact: A compromised template or runtime variable injects hidden instructions before the agent even sees the user task.
risks.mitigation: Treat prompt templates as code, protect them with change control, signing, review, and runtime integrity checks.

risks.name: Unbounded reasoning / denial of wallet
risks.impact: A task triggers excessive token use, repeated retries, or extended reasoning loops that consume cost and capacity.
risks.mitigation: Set token, cost, retry, and reasoning-duration budgets per task and per tenant.

name: Output & Egress Channels
desc: Represents every route through which the agent sends content, files, actions, records, or instructions outward.
core: Generates messages, files, commits, tickets, and summaries
Sends data through chat, email, webhooks, repositories, or APIs
Triggers downstream workflow automation

risks.name: Covert exfiltration through normal output
risks.impact: Sensitive data is hidden inside an ordinary-looking summary, attachment, ticket, or generated file.
risks.mitigation: Inspect outbound content for sensitive data, abnormal destinations, and encoded or transformed payloads.

risks.name: Malicious generated artifact
risks.impact: The agent creates a file, script, link, or pull request that carries harmful behavior into another system.
risks.mitigation: Scan generated artifacts before release and require review for executable or automation-triggering outputs.

risks.name: Downstream automation abuse
risks.impact: A generated record or message triggers CI/CD, ticketing, workflow, or business automation in a way the user did not intend.
risks.mitigation: Apply policy gates at automation boundaries and require explicit approval for actions that can trigger downstream effects.

name: Agent Lifecycle & Governance
desc: Tracks agent inventory, owners, versions, approvals, deployment state, rollback paths, and emergency disablement.
core: Maintains agent inventory, ownership, and version state
Controls promotion from prototype to production
Provides rollback, kill switch, and governance evidence

risks.name: Shadow agents outside governance
risks.impact: Unapproved agents operate outside inventory, monitoring, risk review, and ownership controls.
risks.mitigation: Continuously discover agent workloads and require registration, owner assignment, and risk tiering before production use.

risks.name: Missing kill switch or rollback path
risks.impact: A compromised or misbehaving agent cannot be quickly stopped, isolated, or reverted during an incident.
risks.mitigation: Design emergency disablement, credential revocation, workflow pause, and configuration rollback into the runtime architecture.

risks.name: Untracked agent version drift
risks.impact: Prompts, policies, tools, model versions, and skills drift across environments, making behavior hard to reproduce or secure.
risks.mitigation: Version prompts, tools, models, policies, and skills as release artifacts with promotion controls and change history.

name: Telemetry Integrity & Evidence
desc: Captures tamper-resistant evidence of plans, prompts, retrieved context, tool calls, approvals, outputs, and policy decisions.
core: Records end-to-end agent traces
Protects logs from agent-side modification
Supports audit, replay, non-repudiation, and incident investigation

risks.name: Agent-generated telemetry tampering
risks.impact: A compromised agent alters logs, status reports, or records to hide what it actually did.
risks.mitigation: Write audit events to an append-only external store that agents cannot modify.

risks.name: Incomplete replayability
risks.impact: Investigators cannot reconstruct prompts, retrieved context, tool calls, approvals, or outputs after an incident.
risks.mitigation: Capture structured traces across planning, context retrieval, tool execution, approvals, and egress with sensitive-data controls.

risks.name: Non-repudiation failure
risks.impact: The organization cannot prove which agent, user, policy, or approval caused a high-impact action.
risks.mitigation: Bind actions to signed agent identity, user authority, policy decision, timestamp, and immutable evidence.

name: Guardrails & Monitoring
desc: Policy enforcement, logging, and anomaly detection layered across the whole system.
core: Enforces content and action policies in real time
Logs agent decisions and tool calls for review
Flags anomalous behavior for investigation

risks.name: Guardrail bypass via obfuscation
risks.impact: An attacker phrases a malicious instruction in a way that slips past pattern-based filters while still being understood by the model.
risks.mitigation: Layer semantic and behavioral detection on top of pattern matching, and test guardrails against adversarial phrasing.

risks.name: Blind spots / incomplete logging
risks.impact: Some agent actions or intermediate reasoning steps simply aren't logged, so an incident can't be fully reconstructed after the fact.
risks.mitigation: Log at every hop — planning, tool calls, and inter-agent messages — not just final outputs.

risks.name: Alert fatigue
risks.impact: Too many low-value alerts train reviewers to ignore the monitoring system altogether, including the alerts that matter.
risks.mitigation: Tune alert thresholds to a manageable, high-signal volume and triage by severity.

risks.name: Telemetry tampering / false audit trail
risks.impact: A compromised agent alters logs, status messages, or evidence records to hide what it did or mislead responders.
risks.mitigation: Write logs to append-only systems, preserve chain-of-custody, and verify agent reports against independent telemetry.
